answer: A karst aquifer withdrawal bond ties one identity to one water unit. At the jetty it posts a 40-credit bond and takes one unit from the karst aquifer, sealed to its key and recorded on the basalt ledger. The jetty rejects a reused receipt. The k-th withdrawal pays 5k credits: first 5, tenth 50, hundredth 500. A thousand fakes lock 40,000 and pay 2,502,500, a quadratic total, unmergeable because one receipt serves one key. A rented-withdrawal ring fails the key check and burns its bond. Anyone recomputes fees from the basalt count. An honest identity pays 5 once and recovers 40 when clean.
